tips.title: Local Currency
tips.content: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). Exchange rate ~Rs 300-350 per USD (varies).

tips.title: ATMs
tips.content: Widely available in cities and towns. Major banks: Commercial Bank, HNB, Sampath.

tips.title: Credit Cards
tips.content: Accepted at hotels, restaurants, and shops in tourist areas. Visa and Mastercard most common.

tips.title: Cash vs Card
tips.content: Carry cash for small vendors, tuk-tuks, and rural areas. Cards work in urban centers.

tips.title: Tipping
tips.content: 10% at restaurants, round up for tuk-tuks, Rs 100-500 for guides/porters.

tips.title: West & South Coast
tips.content: December to March (dry season). Best for beaches and hill country.

tips.title: East Coast
tips.content: April to September (dry season). Arugam Bay surfing season May-September.

tips.title: Hill Country
tips.content: December to April for clear skies. Can visit year-round but expect rain other months.

tips.title: Wildlife Safaris
tips.content: February to July (dry season). Animals gather around waterholes.

tips.title: Cultural Triangle
tips.content: Year-round, but November to April is most comfortable (less rain).

tips.title: Tourist SIM Cards
tips.content: Available at airport and mobile shops. Main providers: Dialog, Mobitel, Airtel.

tips.title: Pricing
tips.content: Tourist packages Rs 1,000-2,000 with data (10-50GB) valid 30 days.

tips.title: Coverage
tips.content: Good 4G coverage in cities and towns. 3G in rural areas. Some remote spots have no signal.

tips.title: WiFi
tips.content: Most hotels, guesthouses, and cafes offer free WiFi.

tips.title: ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization)
tips.content: Required for most nationalities. Apply online at eta.gov.lk before arrival.

tips.title: Cost
tips.content: Approximately $50 USD for 30-day tourist visa.

tips.title: Duration
tips.content: 30 days (extendable to 90 days through Department of Immigration).

tips.title: Processing
tips.content: Usually approved within 24-48 hours. Apply at least 3 days before travel.

tips.title: General Safety
tips.content: Sri Lanka is generally safe for tourists. Use common sense and stay aware.

tips.title: Scams
tips.content: Beware of tuk-tuk overcharging, fake gems, and pushy touts. Agree on prices beforehand.

tips.title: Beach Safety
tips.content: Strong currents on some beaches. Swim only where locals swim. Follow warning flags.

tips.title: Wildlife
tips.content: Don't approach wild elephants. Keep 30m distance. Never feed monkeys.

tips.title: Health
tips.content: Drink bottled water. Use mosquito repellent (dengue prevention). Carry basic first aid.

rules.title: Remove Shoes
rules.content: Always remove footwear before entering temples or homes.

rules.title: Dress Modestly
rules.content: Cover shoulders and knees. Some temples provide sarongs. White clothing preferred at some Buddhist temples.

rules.title: No Photos
rules.content: Don't photograph inside shrine rooms without permission. Never pose with back to Buddha statue.

rules.title: Clockwise Walk
rules.content: Walk clockwise around stupas and religious monuments.

rules.title: Be Respectful
rules.content: No public displays of affection. Speak quietly. Don't point feet at Buddha images.

rules.title: Eating with Hands
rules.content: Sri Lankans eat rice and curry with right hand. Left hand is considered unclean.

rules.title: Wash Hands
rules.content: Wash hands before eating. Most restaurants have wash basins.

rules.title: Feet Position
rules.content: Never point feet at food or people while sitting.

rules.title: Try Local Food
rules.content: Rice and curry, hoppers, kottu roti, string hoppers. Ask for mild spice if sensitive.

rules.title: Ask Permission
rules.content: Always ask before photographing people, especially in rural areas.

rules.title: Military & Police
rules.content: Don't photograph military installations, checkpoints, or security personnel.

rules.title: Religious Sites
rules.content: Some temples prohibit photography. Look for signs or ask.

rules.title: Wildlife
rules.content: No flash photography near animals. Can disturb them.

rules.title: Greetings
rules.content: Handshakes common. Ayubowan (ah-yu-bo-wan) means hello/goodbye with hands together.

rules.title: Head & Feet
rules.content: Head is sacred, feet are lowest. Never touch someone's head or point feet at people.

rules.title: Bargaining
rules.content: Expected at markets and with tuk-tuk drivers. Not in fixed-price shops.

rules.title: Public Affection
rules.content: Holding hands okay. Kissing/hugging in public frowned upon.
